rule: Negative subject focus uses the embedded/subjunctive negative aan fused with baa/ayaa rather than ordinary main-clause ma.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (1999), Simple Sentences focus discussion; Heine & Reh (1984), Grammaticalization and Reanalysis in African Languages; John I. Saeed, The Functions of Focus in Somali
note: Unaccented baan is orthographically ambiguous with baa + 1sg aan in other constructions. The project therefore requires an exact reviewed negative predicate before assigning the negative-subject-focus reading.

rule: In focused-subject negative clauses, reviewed simple-past negative verb surfaces may be reused with baan/ayaan when the source paradigm is person-neutral.
source: Saeed focus-negation discussion plus reviewed Qaamuus negative paradigms
project_execution: Only exact morphology records with polarity=negative, tense_aspect=tagto, and person_neutralized=true are executable. No suffix derivation.

rule: Focused-subject negative clauses can use the negative past-progressive form with baan/ayaan; reviewed person-neutral surfaces remain invariant across subject persons.
source: Somali Grammar Revision negative reduced-form discussion plus reviewed Qaamuus negative past-progressive paradigms
project_execution: Only exact morphology records with polarity=negative, tense_aspect=tagto_socota, and person_neutralized=true are executable. No unseen form is generated.

rule: A common-noun subject focused by negative baan/ayaan remains in the absolute/non-subject case, as in affirmative baa/ayaa subject focus. The negative reading is assigned only when the predicate independently supplies reviewed negative evidence.
source: Heine & Reh subject-focus case rule plus Saeed negative-focus rule
note: Do not globally reinterpret baan/ayaan as negative because they can overlap subject-clitic spellings in non-subject focus.
